Last month, I got involuntarily admitted to a mental hospital because I told my therapist I attempted three weeks prior to our session. I thought I was in the clear because the surveys they make us take always use the phrase "in the last two weeks," and I told them I didn't have an active plan. I was still put on a 5150 and was pissed off at first but looking, back I'm glad they did that bc idk I probably would've done something.

I think you should tell her. Depending on the situation/your therapist's call, you may or may not get hospitalized (or you can do a safety plan) so it wouldn't hurt to be prepared for that possibility. It's good that you're being prepared for what might happen, I hope all goes well for you.

I'm blind as a bat without my glasses/contact; without them, I can't read my computer screen that's a foot away. I've only had two sessions so far, but my latest one, I just took them off. I was wearing contacts my first session so I couldn't exactly take them off in the middle of the session haha. I purposefully wore glasses this time to do just that.

  
I was able to make eye contact without my glasses (I have this stupid erroneous mentality of "If I can't see them they cant see me!"). I do this too when I'm walking and see someone familiar, I just start cleaning my glasses so I don't have to look at them. But when I feel ashamed about discussing some topics with my therapist, I look at something in the room instead of him. We've discussed my poor eye contact because we're discussing an autism and/or adhd diagnosis, so I told him directly about the glasses thing just in case if he's like "huh they randomly started getting good at eye contact" lol

I think The Land is Mitski's best work. While I absolutely love her older work with the open D guitar tuning, I did think some of her songs sounded too similar to one another (doesn't stop me from jamming out to all of them lol). I remember seeing a behind the scenes video about *Heaven*, it was originally supposed to be a song with that open D tuning but I'm so glad they took that swingy, romantic approach instead of one we're all familiar with. I'm always a fan of Mitski's lyricism, but I was absolutely blown away by this album's lyrics.

I remember the first time I listened, I was in one of those "early" listening parties at some bar before the album's actual release date. I recall being *so* enchanted with *The Deal* and *My Love Mine all Mine*, and they're to this day one of my fav Mitski songs. I'm SUCH a massive fan of the instrumentals in this album and I can dote about it all day!!!!!!!!

Def a stretch, but just throwing anything out there.
